Hi Aaron —

Thanks for the spreadsheet. See inline answers and an attached two-page summary of our hosted API retention and deletion controls. Highlights:

• Regional placement: Customers on the Hosted API may request their tenant be pinned to a specific cloud region (US, EU). We enforce region pinning at tenant provisioning; data is stored in region-specific object storage and compute.

• Retention windows: By default, request payloads and generated outputs are retained for up to 30 days for service quality and abuse detection. Embeddings are retained for 90 days by default, but customers can request shorter retention or opt-out of embeddings storage.

• Deletion workflow: Customers submit an erasure request via the Console or API. We initiate a prioritized deletion job that removes tenant-level artifacts within 24 hours and purges associated blobs from primary storage within 72 hours. Backups and snapshots are scheduled for deletion in the next available snapshot cycle (up to 30 days) and are cryptographically marked for purge; we provide an audit trail entry once the purge completes.

• Backups & snapshots: Backups are incremental, encrypted, and stored in the same region as the tenant unless a geo-redundancy option is purchased. Snapshot retention is configurable; we honor deletion requests by expiring older snapshots and removing keys to make contents unrecoverable before physical lifecycle reclamation.

• Attestation and logs: We provide an event with a deletion_job_id and timestamp; customers can export audit events via the Console or query via our Events API. For enterprise customers we provide a signed deletion attestation on request.

• Encryption and KMS: Data at rest is encrypted with customer-shared keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private customers. For Hosted, we use provider-managed KMS with envelope encryption; customer-managed keys (BYOK) are available for Enterprise plans. TLS 1.2+ for all in-transit connections.

I've attached a short PDF summarizing the above and a suggested row-by-row answer to your spreadsheet. Happy to join a call later this week to walk the team through details.

Thanks,
Naomi
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Naomi/Ben — I reviewed and made two edits for accuracy; pasted below are the corrected operational commitments and I attached the formal retention summary PDF we can send. Key clarifications:

1) Region pinning — We support per-tenant region pinning at provisioning. Note: certain third-party dependent services (managed logging ingestion, CCaaS integrations) may route metadata to service endpoints in the same cloud provider region family; we call those out on the contract addendum.

2) Retention timing — Default retention for request/response is 30 days. Embeddings default to 90 days. We have an opt-out flag in the Console and at the API level: "store=false" for embedding calls; we log the opt-out event for audit.

3) Deletion guarantees — We guarantee that primary objects are removed within 72 hours of an acknowledged erasure job. Backups are marked for deletion on next snapshot cycle; final physical reclaim can be up to 30 days post-request. This is standard for incremental snapshot-based systems. For customers needing shorter windows we offer a managed purge add-on with SLA.

4) Attestation — We will return a deletion_job_id and link to an Events log entry. For enterprise customers we provide a signed attestation within 5 business days.

5) Keys & encryption — Hosted uses provider KMS by default; we support BYOK for enterprise customers. All keys are rotated per provider recommendations and we store small metadata pointers (not raw keys) in our control plane.

Action: attaching "Redwood_HostedAPI_Data_Retention_Summary_2029-04.pdf" (2 pages) and adding two bullet edits to the draft. Once you approve, Ben, I'll finalize and send to Aaron.

Hi Aaron —

Thanks for sending the spreadsheet and apologies for the delay — appreciate the level of detail. Please find our concise answers below (I've attached a filled spreadsheet and a short two‑page summary for your InfoSec team). If anything needs to be sharpened, flag it and we'll follow up quickly.

Q: Can customer data be pinned to a specific region?
A: Yes. We support tenant-level region pinning at provisioning (US or EU). Data storage and compute for the tenant are constrained to the chosen region.

Q: What are retention windows?
A: Default retention for request payloads and generation outputs is 30 days. Embeddings are retained 90 days by default. Customers can request shorter retention or opt-out for embeddings.

Q: Deletion workflow and timelines?
A: Customers initiate erasure via Console or API. Primary objects removed within 72 hours of job acknowledgement; backups/snapshots marked for purge and deleted on next snapshot cycle (up to 30 days). For enterprise add-on customers we offer accelerated purge SLAs. Deletion completion returns a deletion_job_id and timestamp.

Q: Backups and snapshots — how handled?
A: Incremental, encrypted backups in-region by default; geo-redundancy is an opt-in feature. Snapshots scheduled according to tenant config; when deletion requested we expire keys and schedule snapshot purge.

Q: Attestation, logs, and proof?
A: Events API and Console export provide deletion events and job ids. Signed attestations available on request for enterprise customers within 5 business days.

Q: Encryption & KMS?
A: All data in transit uses TLS; at-rest encryption uses provider-managed KMS by default. BYOK/customer-managed keys supported on Enterprise plans.
